<reason>A razor-thin win for PRO. Both sides executed the format well, answered pressure questions directly with A1/A2 labels, and produced genuine clash rather than ships-passing speeches. A's core coordination argument — that only a universal default ends the grade-wide migration, while design mandates leave the group, the comparison culture, and the exiled child exactly where they are — survived the whole exchange; B's response (design law changes the environment) was real but never fully explained why a chronological feed neutralizes the social pull A identified, and B conceded the lying child gets the adult engine either way. B's best route, the surveillance asymmetry (liability for wrong guesses pressures universal ID checks), was sharp and only partially answered by A's reasonable-steps/offline-analogies reply. B also had to switch schemes mid-debate (minors-only to universal defaults) when A caught the verification contradiction; B defended the move capably, but the shift cost credibility. A's closing crystallized the decisive question more cleanly. Minor execution costs (clipped endings) were roughly even on both sides.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The age-gate exchange: A's Rebuttal 1 caught B needing the same verification B called "catastrophic," forcing B to pivot to universal defaults; B's Rebuttal 2 reply — that a wrong guess costs a wrong default under design law but liability under a ban, creating asymmetric surveillance pressure — was the sharpest single recovery, but A's closing counter (the grade still lives on the platform either way, and B conceded inference is good enough for reasonable-steps enforcement) kept the advantage with A.</best_rebuttal>
